---
title: "Identifying CEOs"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(titleclassifier)
library(dplyr)
# the pipeline steps print a progress line; keep it out of the tables
quiet <- function(x) { utils::capture.output(x <- force(x)); x }
# example titles as a Part VII frame, one person per title
example_frame <- function(titles, pay = 0) {
  d <- titleclassifier::tinypartvii[rep(1, length(titles)), ]
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_TITLE <- titles
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_NAME_PERS <- sprintf("PERSON %02d", seq_along(titles))
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_COMP_ORG <- as.character(pay)
  rownames(d) <- NULL
  d
}
# one hand-built filing: a row per person. boxes: T trustee, O officer,
# K key employee, H highly compensated (none on a 990-EZ)
filing <- function(id, form, people, org.type = NA) {
  d <- titleclassifier::tinypartvii[rep(1, nrow(people)), ]
  d$OBJECTID <- id; d$RETURN_TYPE <- form; d$ORG_NAME_L1 <- id
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_TITLE <- people$title
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_NAME_PERS <- paste(id, seq_len(nrow(people)))
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_AVE_HOUR_WEEK <- as.character(people$hours)
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_AVE_HOUR_WEEK_RL <- "0"
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_COMP_ORG <- as.character(people$pay)
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_COMP_RLTD <- "0"; d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_COMP_OTH <- "0"; d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_EMPL_BEN <- "0"
  b <- if (is.null(people$boxes)) rep("", nrow(people)) else people$boxes
  box <- function(k) if (form == "990EZ") "" else ifelse(grepl(k, b), "X", "")
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_POS_INDIV_TRUST_X <- box("T"); d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_POS_INST_TRUST_X <- ""
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_POS_OFF_X <- box("O"); d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_POS_KEY_EMPL_X <- box("K")
  d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_POS_HIGH_COMP_X <- box("H"); d$F9_07_COMP_DTK_POS_FORMER_X <- ""
  if (!is.na(org.type)) d$org.type <- org.type
  rownames(d) <- NULL
  d
}
p <- function(...) data.frame(..., stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
steps08 <- function(d) quiet(d |> standardize_df() |> remove_dates() |> standardize_conj() |>
  split_titles() |> standardize_spelling() |> gen_status_codes() |> standardize_titles() |>
  categorize_titles())
# a filing's people, before (title only) and after step 09
show <- function(res, id, extra = NULL) {
  r <- res[res$object.id == id & res$role.primary, ]
  r <- r[order(as.integer(sub(".* ", "", r$dtk.name))), ]
  boxes <- with(r, paste0(ifelse(dtk.indiv.trustee.x %in% 1, "T", ""), ifelse(dtk.officer.x %in% 1, "O", ""),
                          ifelse(dtk.key.empl.x %in% 1, "K", ""), ifelse(dtk.high.comp.x %in% 1, "H", "")))
  before <- ifelse(nzchar(r$board.role) & !is.na(r$board.role), paste("BOARD", r$board.role), r$emp.level)
  after  <- ifelse(r$role.final == "BOARD", "BOARD",
            ifelse(r$role.final == "CEO", paste0("**CEO (", r$role.ceo, ")**"), r$role.final))
  out <- data.frame(title = r$title.raw, pay = format(r$tot.comp, big.mark = ","), hours = r$tot.hours,
                    boxes = if (r$formtype[1] == "990EZ") "none" else boxes,
                    `title only` = before, `step 09` = after, check.names = FALSE)
  if (!is.null(extra)) out <- cbind(out, extra(r))
  knitr::kable(out, row.names = FALSE, align = c("l", "r", "r", "l", "l", "l", rep("l", ncol(out) - 6)),
               caption = sprintf("%s: org.type %s; org.leadership %s", id,
                                 ifelse(is.na(r$org.type[1]), "none", r$org.type[1]), r$org.leadership[1]))
}
```

Most research on nonprofit leadership starts with one question per
organization: who is the chief executive? Part VII seldom answers it
directly:
- Many filers list a CEO or executive director.
- Many others list a "President" who may be the paid head or the volunteer
  board chair.
- Some list only board officers and a bookkeeper.
- Some organization types name their chief executive with a title of their
  own: a union's business manager, a club's general manager, a Legion post's
  adjutant.

On 2019-2023 filings that pay anyone, a title alone names the CEO for 64% of
501(c)(3) charities. For unions, lodges, benefit trusts, cemeteries and
veterans posts it names the CEO for only 0-13%.

`titleclassifier` finds the CEO in layers. Each layer is described below, in
the order the pipeline applies it:

```
1. Standard title (step 07)    "Exec. Dir." -> EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR
2. Title level (step 08)       EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR is a CEO-level title
3. Rules (step 09)             designated by title -> imputed from pay ->
                               unpaid full-time leader -> otherwise run by the board
4. CEO thesaurus (step 09)     for 11 organization types, the type's own CEO
                               title, and the stipend titles that are never a CEO
5. 990-EZ (step 09)            no checkboxes: a model replaces the rules,
                               with a guard; the thesaurus still applies
```

The result is in `role.final == "CEO"`, with how the CEO was found in
`role.ceo`, and how the filing is led in `org.leadership`:

| `role.ceo` | The CEO is ... |
|---|---|
| designated | named by a CEO-level title, in an officer position |
| co-ceo | one of two or more designated CEOs |
| interim | designated, with an INTERIM or ACTING status |
| imputed | the highest-paid plausible leader when no title names one, or an unpaid full-time leader |
| thesaurus | the chief-executive title of the organization's type |
| model | named by the 990-EZ role model |

| `org.leadership` | The filing ... |
|---|---|
| designated, thesaurus, imputed, model | has a CEO, found this way |
| board_governed | pays people but has no plausible leader: the board runs it |
| no_paid | pays no one |

## 1. From the title to a CEO-level title

Steps 01 to 07 clean the title and map it to one of a few hundred standard
titles (`title.standard`). Step 08 gives each standard a level. Eight
standards are CEO level:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
tax <- get_title_taxonomy(); xw <- get_title_xwalk()
ceo <- tax$title.standard[tax$emp.level == "CEO"]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  `standard title` = ceo,
  `variants mapped to it` = vapply(ceo, function(s) sum(xw$title.standard == s), 1L),
  examples = vapply(ceo, function(s) { v <- xw$title.variant[xw$title.standard == s]
    paste(head(v[order(nchar(v))], 5), collapse = ", ") }, ""),
  check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

The crosswalk decides what a title means *on its own*. The titles that matter
most for the CEO are the ones it cannot settle:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
x <- c("President & CEO", "Pres/CEO", "Exec. Dir.", "Chief Exec Officer", "Executive Director/Founder",
       "Head of School", "Superintendent", "Senior Pastor", "Associate Pastor",
       "President", "Chairman", "Chancellor", "Director", "Executive Vice President",
       "General Manager", "Business Manager", "Fund Administrator", "Adjutant")
out <- steps08(example_frame(x))
out <- out[order(out$dtk.name, out$title.order), ]
lvl <- ifelse(!is.na(out$board.role) & nzchar(out$board.role), paste("board:", out$board.role), out$emp.level)
knitr::kable(data.frame(`filed title` = out$title.raw, `standard title` = out$title.standard,
                        `level or board role` = lvl, check.names = FALSE), row.names = FALSE)
```

* **PRESIDENT is a board title.** On its own, PRESIDENT maps to BOARD
  PRESIDENT. The crosswalk files the volunteer reading, the more common one
  across all filers. Step 09 decides whether a particular president runs the
  organization.
* **PRESIDENT & CEO collapses to CEO** (step 04). A paired title names the
  CEO outright.
* **CHANCELLOR** is rewritten in step 07: a paid chancellor becomes CEO, an
  unpaid one BOARD PRESIDENT. (These examples are unpaid.)
* **GENERAL MANAGER, BUSINESS MANAGER, FUND ADMINISTRATOR and ADJUTANT** are
  staff or board titles in general. In a club, a union, a benefit trust or a
  veterans post, they name the chief executive. Section 3 handles them.

## 2. The rules

Step 09 (`resolve_roles()`) reads each person's checkboxes, pay and hours
along with the title, and decides the filing's CEO in this order. Each rule
applies only if the earlier ones found no CEO.

1. **Designated.** A person with a CEO-level title is the CEO, unless the
   checkboxes put them on the board only. Two or more designated CEOs are each
   `co-ceo`; a designated CEO with an INTERIM status (INTERIM, ACTING) is
   `interim`.
2. **Imputed from pay.** The highest-paid *plausible leader* is the CEO. A
   plausible leader:
   - is paid;
   - has the officer box, or a leadership title (president, director,
     manager, administrator, chief, ...);
   - works 15+ hours a week or is paid $25,000+;
   - reports at least 5 hours a week, if they report hours at all. Presidents
     are exempt: older filings often show a paid president at 0.1 hours;
   - is not a board chair with the trustee box working under 25 hours a week.
     That pattern is a paid chair, not an executive;
   - does not hold a stipend title in the CEO thesaurus (section 3).
3. **An unpaid full-time leader.** On a full 990, an unpaid person with a
   leader or chair title, 35+ hours a week and the officer box is the CEO
   (`imputed`). The founder-president of an all-volunteer organization and the
   superior of a religious order are examples. If several people tie for the
   most hours, as in a student group whose officers all report 50, no one is
   named.
4. **Otherwise no CEO.** A filing that pays people but has no plausible leader
   is `board_governed`; one that pays no one is `no_paid`.

Two further rules keep stipends from making executives:
- **The stipend rule.** A board title held under 10 hours a week for under
  $25,000 is a board seat, even with the officer box: a titular president
  with a stipend.
- **Past and elect.** A past president or president-elect (a FORMER or FUTURE
  status from step 06) holds a board seat, not the office.

```{r, include = FALSE}
rules_ex <- list(
  filing("A designated", "990", p(
    title = c("President & CEO", "Chair of the Board", "Chief Financial Officer", "Treasurer"),
    pay = c(410000, 0, 260000, 0), hours = c(55, 5, 50, 3), boxes = c("O", "TO", "O", "TO"))),
  filing("B imputed", "990", p(
    title = c("President", "Vice President", "Program Director"),
    pay = c(85000, 0, 42000), hours = c(40, 2, 40), boxes = c("TO", "T", ""))),
  filing("C unpaid full-time", "990", p(
    title = c("President", "Vice President", "Treasurer"),
    pay = c(0, 0, 0), hours = c(45, 5, 3), boxes = c("TO", "TO", "TO"))),
  filing("D board-governed", "990", p(
    title = c("President", "Secretary", "Bookkeeper"),
    pay = c(6000, 0, 18000), hours = c(5, 2, 10), boxes = c("TO", "TO", ""))))
res_rules <- quiet(resolve_roles(steps08(bind_rows(rules_ex))))
```

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_rules, "A designated")
show(res_rules, "B imputed")
show(res_rules, "C unpaid full-time")
show(res_rules, "D board-governed")
```

- **A.** The CEO is designated by title.
- **B.** No title names a CEO, so the paid, full-time president with the
  officer box is imputed. The unpaid vice president is a board seat.
- **C.** Nobody is paid. The president works 45 hours a week with the officer
  box, so the president is the unpaid full-time leader.
- **D.** The president's $6,000 for 5 hours a week is a stipend (the stipend
  rule), and a bookkeeper is not a plausible leader, so the board runs the
  organization.

## 3. Organization types with their own CEO titles

Some kinds of organization name their chief executive with a title the rules
read as something else. Some also pay board officers stipends that the pay
rule mistakes for executive pay. Labeling all five years of 150 organizations
(FINDINGS.md F-031) showed where step 09 picked the wrong person or none. The
**CEO thesaurus** (`ceo.thesaurus`, from
`data-raw/crosswalks/ceo-thesaurus.csv`) records the fixes by organization
type.

### Finding the organization type

`org_types()` gives each filing one of 11 types, or none. It uses, in order of
preference:

1. an `org.type` column you supply (the examples here do this);
2. NTEE code and 501(c) subsection columns joined from the IRS Business
   Master File (for example with `panel990::bmf_retrieve()`), mapped by
   `org_type_from_codes()`;
3. the organization's name and the titles in its Part VII, by
   `org_type_from_name()`.

| Type | From the codes | From the name or titles |
|---|---|---|
| veterans | 501(c)(19), (c)(23) | AMERICAN LEGION, VFW, AMVETS, DAV; an ADJUTANT or QUARTERMASTER on Part VII |
| fraternal | 501(c)(8), (c)(10) | LODGE, ELKS, MASONIC, MOOSE, EAGLES, KNIGHTS OF COLUMBUS, GRANGE; EXALTED RULER, WORSHIPFUL, POTENTATE |
| union | 501(c)(5), NTEE J or none | LOCAL 123, UNION, BROTHERHOOD, TEAMSTERS, IBEW, AFSCME; a BUSINESS AGENT or BUSINESS MANAGER |
| club | 501(c)(7) | COUNTRY, GOLF, YACHT, ATHLETIC, TENNIS or SWIM CLUB |
| coop | 501(c)(12) | COOPERATIVE, CO-OP, ELECTRIC MEMBERSHIP, WATER SUPPLY, TELEPHONE |
| trust | 501(c)(9), (c)(17) | TRUST FUND, WELFARE FUND, PENSION, BENEFIT PLAN, VEBA |
| cemetery | 501(c)(13) | CEMETERY, MEMORIAL PARK, BURIAL |
| university | NTEE B41-B43, not a foundation or alumni group | UNIVERSITY, COLLEGE, SEMINARY |
| ministry | NTEE X | CHURCH, MINISTRY, CONGREGATION, PARISH, DIOCESE; a PASTOR, REVEREND or BISHOP |
| fire | NTEE M24 | FIRE DEPARTMENT, FIRE COMPANY, VOLUNTEER FIRE, HOSE CO |
| orchestra | NTEE A68, A69 | ORCHESTRA, SYMPHONY, PHILHARMONIC |

When codes are present, the subsection settles the membership types: a
501(c)(3) "Union Rescue Mission" is not a union. The name can only add a
type that a missing or wrong NTEE code would have given (university, fire,
orchestra, ministry). The output records the result in `org.type` and its
source in `org.type.source` (supplied, codes, inferred or none).

### The thesaurus entries

Each entry pairs an organization type with a title pattern, matched against
the cleaned title (`title.v7`), and an effect:

* **ceo.** The holder runs that kind of organization, if paid at least
  `min_pay` and working at least `min_hours` a week. Unreported hours do not
  rule a paid holder out.
* **not_ceo.** A holder paid under `min_pay` and, where `min_hours` is set,
  working under `min_hours` a week is on a stipend. They are never made the
  CEO, by title or by pay.
* **outranks.** Titles a `ceo` holder wins over even when the filing
  already has a CEO.

```{r}
th <- get_ceo_thesaurus()
knitr::kable(th[, c("org_type", "title_pattern", "effect", "min_hours", "min_pay", "outranks")])
```

The entries by type:

| Type | Who runs it | Who does not | Board titles to know |
|---|---|---|---|
| **veterans** | the post or department **adjutant**, paid $25k+ for 20+ h/wk | treasurer, finance officer, quartermaster, trustee, secretary or adjutant on a stipend (under $30k and 35 h/wk) | the COMMANDER is the board chair; a DEPARTMENT SENIOR VICE COMMANDER the vice chair |
| **fraternal** | no single title: usually a paid executive or none | the lodge **secretary, recorder or treasurer** on a stipend (under $40k and 35 h/wk) | EXALTED RULER, WORSHIPFUL MASTER and POTENTATE are the chair; wardens, rabbans and knights are members |
| **club** | the **general manager** (or club manager, GM), $25k+ and 20+ h/wk; outranks a better-paid superintendent, golf pro, chef, controller or "director of" | a **pool, snack, canteen, bar or grounds manager** paid under $25k | the PRESIDENT is the board chair |
| **coop** | the **general manager**, $25k+ and 20+ h/wk | | |
| **trust** | the **fund, plan, trust or benefits administrator**, $25k+ and 20+ h/wk | | the CHAIRMAN and TRUSTEES are the board |
| **union** | the **business manager**, $25k+ and 20+ h/wk; outranks a paid **president** | | the PRESIDENT is the board chair even when paid |
| **university** | the **president**, $50k+ and 20+ h/wk; outranks a chancellor, provost or vice president | | the board CHAIR |
| **ministry** | the **senior, lead, general or head pastor**, a **bishop**, **overseer**, **rabbi** or **rector**, 20+ h/wk, **paid or not**; an associate or youth pastor does not match | | |
| **fire** | the paid full-time **fire chief** ($25k+, 20+ h/wk) | the company's **secretary or treasurer** on part-time pay (under $40k and 35 h/wk) | |
| **cemetery** | | an **unpaid superintendent** | |
| **orchestra** | no entry: an executive director or president & CEO usually names the CEO | | |

### How an entry is applied

1. **not_ceo** titles are removed from the running before the rules: they
   are not designated and not imputed.
2. The rules of section 2 run.
3. The best-paid holder of a **ceo** title becomes the CEO
   (`role.ceo = "thesaurus"`) in three cases:
   - the filing has no CEO;
   - its CEO was only imputed from pay or named by the 990-EZ model;
   - its CEO's title is one the entry outranks.

   A CEO designated by a CEO-level title, such as an executive director,
   stays the CEO.

```{r, include = FALSE}
types_ex <- list(
  filing("Club", "990", p(
    title = c("President", "General Manager", "Golf Course Superintendent", "Treasurer"),
    pay = c(0, 180000, 210000, 0), hours = c(3, 50, 50, 2), boxes = c("TO", "K", "H", "TO")), "club"),
  filing("Union local", "990", p(
    title = c("President", "Business Manager", "Recording Secretary"),
    pay = c(160000, 150000, 8000), hours = c(40, 50, 5), boxes = c("TO", "O", "TO")), "union"),
  filing("Legion department", "990", p(
    title = c("Department Commander", "Department Adjutant", "Treasurer"),
    pay = c(0, 48000, 60000), hours = c(10, 40, 40), boxes = c("TO", "O", "O")), "veterans"),
  filing("Lodge", "990", p(
    title = c("Exalted Ruler", "Secretary", "Treasurer"),
    pay = c(0, 24000, 3000), hours = c(5, 20, 3), boxes = c("TO", "O", "O")), "fraternal"),
  filing("Pension fund", "990", p(
    title = c("Real Estate Manager", "Fund Administrator", "Chairman"),
    pay = c(120000, 95000, 0), hours = c(40, 40, 2), boxes = c("K", "K", "T")), "trust"),
  filing("University", "990", p(
    title = c("Vice President for Advancement", "President", "Chair"),
    pay = c(300000, 280000, 0), hours = c(50, 50, 2), boxes = c("O", "TO", "TO")), "university"),
  filing("Church", "990", p(
    title = c("Senior Pastor", "Chair", "Treasurer"),
    pay = c(0, 0, 0), hours = c(50, 2, 2), boxes = c("T", "T", "T")), "ministry"))
ex_types <- steps08(bind_rows(types_ex))
res_types <- quiet(resolve_roles(ex_types))
# the same filings with the thesaurus switched off
without_thesaurus <- function(d) {
  orig <- get("get_ceo_thesaurus", asNamespace("titleclassifier"))
  utils::assignInNamespace("get_ceo_thesaurus", function() NULL, "titleclassifier")
  on.exit(utils::assignInNamespace("get_ceo_thesaurus", orig, "titleclassifier"))
  quiet(resolve_roles(d))
}
res_types$rules.only <- without_thesaurus(ex_types)$role.final
was <- function(r) data.frame(`without the thesaurus` = r$rules.only, check.names = FALSE)
```

Each example filing is run twice: as is, and with the thesaurus switched off
(the rules of section 2 alone).

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_types, "Club", was)
```

**Club.** The golf course superintendent is the best-paid person, so pay
alone would make the superintendent the CEO. The general manager runs the
club, and the club entry ranks the general manager above the
superintendent.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_types, "Union local", was)
```

**Union local.** A union president is often paid, and here earns more than
the business manager. The president is still the elected chair. The business
manager runs the local, and the union entry ranks them above the president.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_types, "Legion department", was)
```

**Veterans.** The department adjutant runs the department. The treasurer is
better paid, so pay alone would pick the treasurer. The commander is the
board chair.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_types, "Lodge", was)
```

**Lodge.** The secretary has the officer box and $24,000 for 20 hours a week:
enough for the pay rule to name a CEO. In a lodge that is a stipend. The
fraternal entry keeps the secretary from being the CEO, and the lodge is run
by its board. Before this entry, lodge secretaries were made CEO from pay 91
times in the 2019-2023 sample.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_types, "Pension fund", was)
```

**Benefit trust.** The fund administrator runs the trust. Without the
thesaurus, pay picks the better-paid real estate manager: the title holds
MANAGER, a leadership word, even though the title is uncoded.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_types, "University", was)
```

**University.** The president runs the university. Pay alone favors whoever
earns most, here a vice president.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
show(res_types, "Church", was)
```

**Church.** A senior pastor runs the church whether paid or not. Here the
pastor is unpaid and has only the trustee box, so neither the pay rule nor
the unpaid full-time rule applies.

### How much it helps

The type-specific labels (FINDINGS.md F-031 to F-033) cover 750 filings of
150 organizations from 2019-2023. The table gives the share of filings where
step 09 names the right chief executive (or rightly names none):

| Stratum | Before (F-031) | Rules fixed (F-032) | With the thesaurus (F-033) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| All 750 filings | 80.9% | 85.1% | **87.6%** |
| University | 54% | 78% | 82% |
| Veterans post | 54% | 60% | 66% |
| Club or co-op | 74% | 84% | 92% |
| Lodge | 86% | 86% | 92% |
| Ministry | 88% | 88% | 96% |
| Benefit trust or cemetery | 84% | 84% | 90% |

The thesaurus entries were written from these labels. On 126 held-out filings
from 64 organizations of the same types, the share rose from 79.4% to 81.7%.
The gain is about the same size as in the sample, and comes mostly from
lodges.

### Known limits

- **A paid chancellor.** Step 07 rewrites a paid CHANCELLOR to the title CEO
  before the thesaurus sees it. The university entry's `outranks` then cannot
  match the chancellor, so a paid chancellor stays the designated CEO even
  when a paid president is listed.
- **Two-pastor churches.** ASSOCIATE PASTOR maps to the CEO-level standard
  PASTOR. A church with a senior and an associate pastor therefore gets two
  co-CEOs. The thesaurus does not split them, because both are designated by
  title.
- **Combined titles.** The union pattern misses compressed titles such as
  BMFINSEC (business manager and financial secretary).
- **Former and interim CEOs** who served part of the year can be named
  alongside the current CEO. Telling them apart needs the tax period's dates.

## 4. The 990 and 990-EZ divide

Smaller organizations file the 990-EZ. Its Part VII lists the same people,
titles, pay and hours, but **not the position checkboxes**: no trustee,
officer, key employee or highly compensated box. In 2022, 990-EZ filings
supplied 1.2 million of the 5.1 million Part VII rows.

Most of the rules lean on those boxes:

| Rule | On a full 990 | On a 990-EZ |
|---|---|---|
| Position | from the boxes | from the title and pay alone |
| Designated | a CEO-level title, unless the boxes say board only | a CEO-level title |
| Imputed from pay | needs the officer box **or** a leadership title | needs a leadership title: a paid treasurer who runs the organization is missed |
| Unpaid full-time leader | needs the officer box | never applies |
| Stipend rule | a board title under 10 h/wk and $25k is a board seat | the same, read from the title, since there is no trustee box |

Without the boxes, the rules miss most officers and call too many people
staff. On the 40 hand-labeled 990-EZ people, the rules get 82.5% of roles
right. So on a 990-EZ, step 09 does three things:

1. **The model replaces the rules.** When the xgboost package is installed,
   each person's role on a 990-EZ comes from the no-checkbox role model
   (section 5). `role.method` is `model`.
2. **A guard on the model's CEO.** If the model names as CEO someone with no
   CEO-level title who works under 20 hours a week for under $50,000, the
   person keeps the role the rules give instead. On the labeled filings, those
   model CEOs were mostly stipend-paid officers of board-run organizations.
3. **The thesaurus still applies.** It overrides the model's CEO in the same
   cases as above, so a club's general manager outranks a golf professional
   whom the model would pick.

With the model, 92.5% of the labeled 990-EZ people get the right role. On
23,931 people at organizations that switched between the forms, the model
agrees with their full-990-year role 95.0% of the time, against 92.0% for
the rules. Use `resolve_roles(use_model = FALSE)` to use the rules
everywhere.

## 5. The role model

The model is a classifier trained to answer one question: what would the
checkboxes have said? It predicts each person's role (BOARD, CEO, OFFICER,
MANAGER, PROFESSIONAL or STAFF) from what a 990-EZ does report.

* **Teacher.** About 557,000 people on full-990 filings from 2019-2023, each
  labeled with the role the rules give them *with* the boxes. The boxes are
  then hidden from the model.
* **990-EZ examples.** 20,800 people at organizations that switched forms,
  labeled with their role in the full-990 year.
* **Features.** 100 per person, built by `role_model_features()`:
  - title keywords (PRESIDENT, TREASURER, DIRECTOR, PASTOR, ...);
  - the title's level, board role, domain and SOC group from the taxonomy;
  - pay and hours;
  - the person's rank and share of the filing's pay and hours;
  - the filing's make-up: how many people, how many paid, how many other CEO
    and board titles;
  - status flags.
* **Model.** Gradient-boosted decision trees (xgboost), shipped in
  `inst/extdata/role-model/`. See [Rules and models](classifiers.html).

In effect the model has learned from full-990 filers what a paid person's
situation implies about the boxes. In a small filing where the board is
unpaid, the one person paid for real hours almost always ticks the officer
box and runs the organization, whatever their title says. A board officer on
a small stipend almost always ticks only the trustee box.

```{r, include = FALSE}
ez_ex <- list(
  filing("EZ-1 paid treasurer", "990EZ", p(
    title = c("Treasurer", "President", "Secretary"), pay = c(30000, 0, 0), hours = c(25, 4, 2))),
  filing("EZ-2 stipend president", "990EZ", p(
    title = c("President", "Vice President", "Treasurer"), pay = c(30000, 0, 0), hours = c(10, 2, 2))),
  filing("EZ-3 part-time coordinator", "990EZ", p(
    title = c("Coordinator", "President", "Secretary"), pay = c(18000, 0, 0), hours = c(15, 4, 2))),
  filing("EZ-4 club", "990EZ", p(
    title = c("Golf Professional", "General Manager", "President"), pay = c(60000, 45000, 0),
    hours = c(40, 40, 3)), "club"))
ex_ez <- steps08(bind_rows(ez_ex))
res_ez <- quiet(resolve_roles(ex_ez))
res_ez$rules.only <- quiet(resolve_roles(ex_ez, use_model = FALSE))$role.final
has_model <- !is.null(predict_roles(ex_ez[1, ]))
if (has_model) {
  # the model's own probability that each person is the CEO
  f <- system.file("extdata", "role-model", package = "titleclassifier")
  fit <- xgboost::xgb.load(file.path(f, "role-model.ubj"))
  fn <- readLines(file.path(f, "feature-names.txt"))
  X <- role_model_features(ex_ez)
  miss <- setdiff(fn, colnames(X))
  if (length(miss)) X <- cbind(X, matrix(0, nrow(X), length(miss), dimnames = list(NULL, miss)))
  pr <- predict(fit, xgboost::xgb.DMatrix(X[, fn, drop = FALSE]))
  if (is.null(dim(pr))) pr <- matrix(pr, ncol = 6, byrow = TRUE)
  res_ez$p.ceo <- pr[, 2]
  res_ez$raw.model <- c("BOARD", "CEO", "OFFICER", "MANAGER", "PROFESSIONAL", "STAFF")[max.col(pr, ties.method = "first")]
}
cmp <- function(r) {
  out <- data.frame(`rules alone` = r$rules.only, check.names = FALSE)
  if (has_model) { out$`model's pick` <- r$raw.model; out$`P(CEO)` <- sprintf("%.2f", r$p.ceo) }
  out
}
```

Four 990-EZ filings show where the model changes the CEO, and where step 09
holds it back. `rules alone` is `use_model = FALSE`. `model's pick` is the
model's raw prediction, before the guard and the thesaurus. `P(CEO)` is the
model's probability that the person is the CEO.

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = has_model}
show(res_ez, "EZ-1 paid treasurer", cmp)
```

**The model adds a CEO.** The treasurer is the only paid person, at $30,000
for 25 hours a week. TREASURER is not a leadership title, so the rules cannot
impute a CEO: the treasurer is STAFF and the filing has no CEO. In full-990
data, an organization's only paid person, working real hours while the board
is unpaid, nearly always has the officer box and runs the organization. The
model makes the treasurer the CEO.

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = has_model}
show(res_ez, "EZ-2 stipend president", cmp)
```

**The model removes a CEO.** The president is paid $30,000 for 10 hours a
week. That is over the pay rule's $25,000, and just over the stipend rule's
limits, so the rules impute the president as CEO. On full 990s, a president
paid like this for so few hours, in a filing with no one else paid, mostly
ticks only the trustee box: a board chair with a stipend. The model reads the
president as a board seat, and the filing as run by its board.

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = has_model}
show(res_ez, "EZ-3 part-time coordinator", cmp)
```

**The guard holds the model back.** The model leans toward naming the only
paid person as CEO: a coordinator, here, at $18,000 for 15 hours a week. But
the coordinator has no CEO-level title and works under 20 hours a week for
under $50,000. The guard keeps the rules' answer, STAFF, and the filing has
no CEO.

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = has_model}
show(res_ez, "EZ-4 club", cmp)
```

**The thesaurus overrides the model.** The model picks the best-paid person,
the golf professional. This is a club, and the club entry ranks the general
manager above a golf pro.

```{r, echo = FALSE, eval = !has_model, results = "asis"}
cat("*The model examples need the xgboost package, which was not installed when this page was built.*")
```

The model's limits are the teacher's:
- **It inherits the rules' errors.** It learned from the rules applied to
  full-990 filings, so it repeats what the rules get wrong there.
- **It does not know organization types.** That is why the thesaurus runs
  after it.
- **It is less transparent than a rule.** To see why it decided, compare
  `role.method` and run `resolve_roles(use_model = FALSE)` on the same rows.

## Putting it together

```{r}
data(tinypartvii)
set.seed(11)
df <- dplyr::sample_n(tinypartvii, 1500) |>
  standardize_df() |> remove_dates() |> standardize_conj() |> split_titles() |>
  standardize_spelling() |> gen_status_codes() |> standardize_titles() |>
  categorize_titles() |> conditional_logic()

# one row per filing: how it is led
df |> dplyr::distinct(object.id, formtype, org.leadership) |> dplyr::count(formtype, org.leadership)

# the CEOs, with how each was found
df |> dplyr::filter(role.primary, role.final == "CEO") |>
  dplyr::count(formtype, role.ceo, role.method)
```
